artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Mental Notes," released in July 1975, is the debut album by New Zealand rock band Split Enz. The album showcases a blend of rock with strong influences from art rock and progressive rock, characterized by complex arrangements, theatrical vocals, and a distinctive use of keyboards and guitar textures. Its style reflects the band's early experimental approach, combining pop sensibilities with progressive and contemporary rock elements, setting the foundation for their evolving sound.

As the first full-length release under the Split Enz name (the band was originally called Split Ends), "Mental Notes" holds a significant place in their discography as the starting point of their artistic identity. While not a major commercial success at the time, the album received critical recognition for its ambitious musicality and originality. It established Split Enz as a unique voice in the Australasian rock scene and laid the groundwork for their later, more commercially successful albums.
